clauses.reason: The opening paragraph finds that the actions and policies of the Government of Iran are an unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security, foreign policy and economy of the United States and declares a national emergency to deal with it. No end date, condition or sunset appears in this clause and no held instrument ends it. It is operative on 2026-10-14. Record read for context, not used as the registered basis because its bytes are held only by hash: 31 CFR 560.106 (eCFR, amended through 2026-11-06, in force on 2026-10-14): any action the Secretary of the Treasury is authorized to take under E.O. 12957, 12959, 13059 and later orders relating to the national emergency declared in E.O. 12957 may be taken by OFAC. The sixteen held annual continuation notices from March 2011 to March 2026 (the earlier yearly notices are not held for this order) each continue the emergency declared in this order beyond March 15 of the year; the last, the notice of March 2, 2026 (91 FR 10937), continues it beyond March 15, 2026, which covers 2026-10-14. Executive Order 14382 of February 6, 2026 recites the emergency declared in this order as continuing. The held chain starts in 2011; notices for 1996 to 2010 are not registered as evidence in this packet, which is a gap in the history, not in the 2026 coverage.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12957 (60 FR 14615, March 17, 1995) declares a national emergency about Iran, bars United States persons from contracts for developing or financing Iranian petroleum resources, and authorizes the Treasury to implement. Executive Order 12959 (May 6, 1995) revoked sections 1 and 2 only 'to the extent inconsistent' and says it supplements this order; Executive Order 13059 (August 19, 1997) consolidated the Iran measures but its text revokes nothing in this order. Pub. L. 109-293 section 101 (2006) provides that sanctions under sections 1 and 3 of this order as in effect on January 1, 2006 remain in effect until the President terminates them, and no termination is held. Sixteen yearly continuation notices (2011 to 2026) show the emergency continued beyond March 15, 2026, and Executive Order 14382 (February 2026) recites it. The OFAC regulations in the eCFR (amended through 2026-11-06) cite this order as authority. The order is claimed as in force on 2026-10-14. The history of notices for 1996 to 2010 is not registered in this packet.
Earlier end: Earlier-end test: the order has no own-terms end; its only held later instruments naming it as affected are Executive Order 12959 section 5 (conditional partial revocation of sections 1 and 2) and Executive Order 13059 (consolidating order that revokes other orders), and the yearly continuation notices keep the emergency alive.
Current basis: Current predicate: see the clause's basis. The bounded searches current-law:usc (3 hits), current-law:ecfr (13 hits, the OFAC regulations that cite this order) and later-events:ofr_catalog (26 hits: the two partial revocations, the yearly notices and later Iran orders) found no instrument ending the clause.

Neither is adopted as an end because no source shows an inconsistent part or an extinguished command.
